task_instance: Produce an Arch Linux triage report for a concrete scenario: after `pacman -Syu` upgraded the kernel and the nvidia driver package, the system boots to a black screen because sddm.service fails (nvidia-drm module mismatch with the new kernel). Deliverable: a triage-report.md following the skill's required Output Format (Summary, Triage Steps, Remediation Commands, Validation, Rollback/Cleanup) with copy-paste-ready pacman/systemctl/journalctl commands.
evidence: Wrote triage-report.md in the work directory containing all five required sections with real Arch/systemd commands (pacman -Q/-U/-S, mkinitcpio -P, systemctl daemon-reload/restart/set-default/enable/--failed/is-active/list-dependencies, journalctl -b/-p/-u/-k, paccache -rk2). Verified deliverable two ways: (1) extracted all 15 bash code blocks from the report with a small python script and ran `bash -n` on each -> all 15 passed syntax checking with zero errors; (2) cross-checked the systemctl/journalctl flags actually used (--failed, is-active, daemon-reload, list-dependencies, -b, -p, -u, -k) against the real `systemctl --help` / `journalctl --help` output on this box (systemd 255 is installed here even though this is Ubuntu 24.04, not Arch, and not running as PID 1) confirming every flag exists and is spelled correctly. pacman itself is not installed/runnable in this Ubuntu sandbox, so live execution against a real Arch package database was not possible, but the skill's core deliverable -- an accurate, well-formed, copy-paste-ready triage plan/document -- was produced and verified, matching the skill's actual invocation pattern (an advisory/authoring skill, not one that requires the invoking machine itself to be Arch).
